task.text:
[0] The experimental results showed a reduction of > 20% in the life span of taus/+ animals in light-dark 14:10 conditions compared with the other 2 genotypes.

[1] The life span of male and female hamsters from three genotypes (wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous tau mutants) was recorded in constant darkness. Male and female homozygous mutant hamsters lived significantly longer rather than shorter compared to wild-types.

[2] The life span of male and female hamsters from three genotypes (wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous tau mutants) was recorded in constant darkness. Male and female homozygous mutant hamsters lived significantly longer rather than shorter compared to wild-types.

[3] n=120-190 Flies overexpressing the CYB5R gene (CG5946; CYB5R-OE) were created and validated by showing an approximately twofold increase in CYB5R enzymatic activity in male CYB5R-OE versus control (CT) flies. The log-rank test indicated that male CYB5R-OE flies lived longer with a 10.59% increase in mean lifespan, 10.67% extension in 20% survival (P=0.011, χ2=10.6), and 8.1% increase in 10% survival (P=0.0142, χ2=6).

[4] n=120-140 The compound RU486 induced a twofold increase in CYB5R messenger RNA levels versus vehicle-treated CTs (0.92±0.08 vs. 0.47±0.06, P=0.004), which translated into significant increase in both mean and maximum lifespan when given to young flies (P=0.0008).

[5] A reduction in longevity was observed when flies in the transitional and senescence stages were treated with RU486 to induce CYB5R (P=0.00375, χ2=8.4 and P=0.0413, χ2=4.2 for transitional and senescence stage, respectively).

[6] n=89-147 A reduction in longevity was observed when flies in the transitional and senescence stages were treated with RU486 to induce CYB5R (P=0.00375, χ2=8.4 and P=0.0413, χ2=4.2 for transitional and senescence stage, respectively).

[7] n=160-210 A fat body-specific expression of the CYB5R gene was sufficient to increase mean lifespan in male but not female flies (P=0.00045).

[8] n=120-220 Female CYB5R-OE flies exhibited a 17.47% increase in mean lifespan, 18.50% extension in 20% survival (P=2.27e−05, χ2=17.9) and 17.2% increase in 10% survival (P=0.0011, χ2=10.6).

[9] n=160-210 A fat body-specific expression of the CYB5R gene was sufficient to increase mean lifespan in male but not female flies (P=0.00045).

Each numbered passage describes one lifespan experiment. For each, report three things using ONLY that passage:
  organism: the model organism studied, one lowercase word
  direction: exactly one of 'increases lifespan', 'decreases lifespan', or 'no change'
  method: how the gene was altered, e.g. gene knockout, overexpression, mutation, knockdown

Output one block per passage, in order, formatted exactly:
[0]
organism: ...
direction: ...
method: ...

Nothing else. If a passage does not state something, write 'unstated'.
